1.explanation: Prism’s Java grammar is built on top of the generic C-like grammar (prism-clike.js), which defines the generic "class-name" pattern for capitalized identifiers. The Java language file (prism-java.js) extends and overrides parts of the C-like grammar, but its import-statement pattern does not include matching for class names in the import path. As a result, "UUID" in an import statement is left unclassified. Updating the class-name definitions or the import pattern in these two files (and re-building their minified counterparts) will allow Prism to correctly tokenize UUID as a class-name.
1.bug_scenario: When using Prism to highlight Java code that contains an import statement for a class whose name is all uppercase (e.g. “import java.util.UUID;”), the identifier “UUID” is not being tokenized as a class-name. Instead it renders as plain text. By comparison, GitHub’s highlighter (and Prism’s own definition for other languages) treats UUID as a class-name token.

2.explanation: The Java-specific grammar is defined in components/prism-java.js (and its minified counterpart). In that file the import and package patterns only assign a ‘punctuation’ token to the dots, leaving all identifier segments unstyled. To highlight UUID as a class name, the inside:{ } of the import pattern needs to be extended to include a ‘class-name’ rule for the last segment. The composite prism.js bundle also contains the same Java grammar and will need updating once the component is fixed.
2.bug_scenario: When Prism 1.27.0 highlights a Java import statement such as “import java.util.UUID;” it only tokenizes the punctuation (the dots) as namespace separators. The actual package and class name segments (including “UUID”) are left as plain text instead of being marked with the “class-name” token, so UUID does not receive the correct styling.
